claims.claim: **First-line maintenance:** olaparib is for BRCA-mutated (germline or somatic), FIGO stage III or IV, high-grade serous cancer of the ovary, fallopian tube or peritoneum that has responded, completely or partially, to first-line platinum chemotherapy.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **First-line duration:** stop at 2 years if there is a complete response (no disease on imaging). If disease is still visible but stable at 2 years, the clinician may continue when further benefit is expected.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Maintenance after relapse:** for BRCA-mutated high-grade serous disease that relapsed but stayed platinum-sensitive and is responding after at least two platinum-containing regimens. No data support giving olaparib maintenance again after a later relapse.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Wait for blood counts to recover** from earlier chemotherapy before starting olaparib.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Olaparib tablets 300 mg (2 × 150 mg) by mouth twice daily**, continuously until progression or unacceptable toxicity; taking it with food can reduce nausea. PBS authority; 100 mg and 150 mg tablets.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Metoclopramide 10 mg as needed** (no more than 30 mg in 24 hours, for up to 5 days) is supplied at the start. Nausea can be moderate in the first month or months but usually settles with antiemetics and reassurance, without dose changes.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Dose steps for blood toxicity go 300, then 250, then 200 mg twice daily, then stop.** For ANC under 1.0 or platelets under 75, delay until recovery; the first episode restarts at 300 mg and each later one a step lower. For grade 3 or 4 anaemia, delay until haemoglobin is above 9 g/dL.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Kidney:** with eGFR 31 to 50, reduce to 200 mg twice daily and monitor; it has not been studied below 30. **Liver:** no change for mild or moderate impairment; not recommended in severe impairment.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **MDS and AML:** PARP inhibitors may increase the risk of myelodysplastic syndrome and acute myeloid leukaemia, so check a full blood count with film regularly. Do not give olaparib to anyone with a history of bone marrow dysplasia.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Bloods:** LFTs, FBC and EUC/eGFR at baseline, monthly through the first year, then as indicated.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Pneumonitis, occasionally fatal:** with new or worsening breathlessness, cough, fever or a radiological abnormality, withhold olaparib and investigate promptly; stop it if pneumonitis is confirmed.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Wound healing:** pause olaparib around major surgery and restart once healing is judged adequate.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Fatigue** is common early and usually eases. Exclude other causes and advise graded exercise; if it stays severe despite breaks, consider a short interruption or a lower dose.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hepatitis B screening is not routinely needed** but can be considered in high-risk people. The safety of live vaccines during and after olaparib is not established.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **SOLO1 (first-line maintenance, 391 BRCA-mutated patients):** after 5 years' follow-up, median PFS was 56.0 months with olaparib against 13.8 months with placebo (HR 0.33), and 48.3% against 20.5% were free of progression at 5 years.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **SOLO1 at 7 years:** 67.0% were alive with olaparib against 46.5% with placebo (HR 0.55). The gain is clinically meaningful but missed the trial's prespecified significance threshold.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **SOLO2 (platinum-sensitive relapse, 295 BRCA-mutated patients):** median PFS 19.1 against 5.5 months (HR 0.30). At final analysis, median overall survival was 51.7 against 38.8 months (HR 0.74, p=0.054).
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Harms in SOLO2:** grade 3 to 4 anaemia in 21% on olaparib. Treatment-emergent events led to interruption in 50%, dose reduction in 28% and stopping in 17%, and 5 patients (3%) died of treatment-related MDS or AML.
